problem: Language instructions for navigation are ambiguous or verbose, and image-goal instructions lack intermediate cues and need many pre-captured goal images. No prior navigation task uses a visual prompt on a top-view map as the sole instruction.
motivation: Users need a friendly and precise way to specify navigation routes. A top-view map with a drawn trajectory keeps the full spatial layout, can be built once and reused across episodes, and lets non-experts click or draw a route without writing text.
key_idea: Replace language instructions with a trajectory drawn as arrows on a 2D top-view map, and train a DUET/ETPNav-style navigator (VPNet) that encodes the map with a ViT.
insight: Trajectory-centered cropping and drawn trajectory lines matter most: the uncropped map (a) gets 33.94 SR on val unseen, and lines-only (e) gets 65.92 versus 65.36 for lines plus text (d). Data scale and diversity drive most of the gain: adding PREVALENT and ScaleVLN episodes lifts val-unseen SR from 51.23 to 65.92 to 96.68, and prompt rotation (86.33 to 96.41 SR) helps far more than random agent heading (88.18). Caveat: the test set is derived from ScaleVLN predictions rather than ground-truth trajectories, so the ~97% SR is not directly comparable to VLN numbers.
method: Visual prompt construction: Render a 2D top-view map per MP3D scene, draw arrows connecting the trajectory viewpoints, crop a square around the trajectory with a 60px margin, then tightly crop non-black pixels, giving R2R-VP and R2R-CE-VP.

ViT prompt encoder + OAFC: Each map is resized to 224x224 and encoded by ViT-B/16. For multi-floor trajectories, Order-Aware Floor Concatenation adds a traversal-order embedding to each floor's features and concatenates them.

Topological mapping and node embedding: The agent builds an online topology graph. Nodes combine panoramic view features (visual, direction and navigability embeddings, 2-layer transformer), a step embedding and a position embedding, plus a stop node.

Graph-aware cross-modal encoder: Cross-attention between graph nodes and prompt tokens, then graph-aware self-attention with a pairwise distance bias. A local branch is fused dynamically for discrete DUET-style prediction; only the global graph encoder is used for continuous ETPNav-style prediction with a waypoint predictor.
Trajectory-level augmentation: Add in-domain PREVALENT episodes (MP3D) and out-of-domain ScaleVLN episodes (523 HM3D scenes, first floor only), converted to visual prompts.
View-level augmentation: Randomly rotate prompt maps by 0, π/2, π or 3π/2, and sample the agent's initial heading from [0, 2π). This is valid because the heading is independent of the prompt.
Training: A weighted mix of behavior cloning and DAgger losses with λ=0.5, trained for 400k iterations.

setting.backbone: DUET-based (discrete) and ETPNav-based (continuous) VPNet with ViT-B/16 (ImageNet-21k) encoders, trained end-to-end
setting.training_data: R2R-VP / R2R-CE-VP train, plus PREVALENT-derived episodes (177,134 discrete; 88,694 continuous) and ScaleVLN-derived episodes (1,600,945 over 523 HM3D scenes, discrete only)
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB views plus a 2D top-view map with the visual prompt as the instruction
setting.action_space: Discrete: topological graph node selection. Continuous: waypoints from a pretrained waypoint predictor, executed in Habitat
setting.privileged: Ground-truth trajectory drawn on a top-view map (as the instruction); top-view maps of the scene built from MP3D meshes, with poorly reconstructed floors and scenes excluded

numbers_note: Benchmarks are the paper's new R2R-VP and R2R-CE-VP datasets, so they are listed as 'other:'. There are no OSR or TL values for the continuous setting. Val/test sets have slightly fewer episodes than the official R2R splits.
results: With PREVALENT and ScaleVLN augmentation, VPNet reaches 96.68 SR on R2R-VP val unseen and 97.56 on test. This is far above VPNet trained on R2R alone (51.23) and above DUET on language instructions with the same data (SR 81 on val unseen). In continuous environments, VPNet (R2R+PRE) reaches 47.96 SR on val unseen, below ETPNav with language (57), and 84.11 on val seen.
limitations: The instruction is a ground-truth trajectory drawn on a top-view map, which is much more informative than language and requires a map of the scene; the VLN comparison is therefore not like-for-like.
Continuous-setting performance on unseen scenes (47.96 SR) is weaker than language-based ETPNav, and the work is entirely simulated with no real-robot experiments.
Scenes and floors with poor top-view reconstruction are excluded, and the test set is built from ScaleVLN predictions rather than human-annotated paths.
